key_insight: Radiation-induced grain-boundary segregation in dilute Ni alloys is solute-specific: Fe depletes via vacancy exchange, Cr shows temperature-dependent competition between defect-mediated fluxes, and Mn enriches mainly from thermodynamic driving forces.
engineering_relevance: These mechanisms help predict and control grain-boundary chemistry in Ni-based reactor materials, improving resistance to irradiation damage and long-term structural degradation.
method: Ni2+ ion irradiation of dilute Ni-Fe, Ni-Cr, and Ni-Mn alloys at 500, 800, and 1000 K to 2 dpa
STEM-EDS measurement of grain-boundary composition, including depth-dependent analysis along the same GB
Rate-theory phase-field modeling informed by atomistic transport data
evidence_signal: The study combines systematic irradiation experiments with STEM-EDS and modeling, showing temperature-dependent segregation trends plus void formation and grain-boundary migration effects.
watch_item: Interpretation of grain-boundary chemistry must account for concurrent vacancy/interstitial transport, thermodynamics, voids, and GB migration, which can confound simple segregation models.
paper_title: Deconvoluting Mechanisms of Radiation-Induced Grain Boundary Segregation in Dilute Ni-X (X = Fe, Cr, Mn) Alloys via Ion Irradiation and Phase-field Modeling
